title: Handle incomplete streams and graceful resume for hosted SSE
creator: Aisha Verma
description: Multiple customers reported truncated or missing final tokens when using the Hosted API streaming (SSE) endpoint. Symptoms include streams that end without a final 'done' event, partial JSON payloads, and clients that cannot resume or reassemble the last chunk. Several reports came through Priority Support and two escalations to CSMs for production outages. This ticket tracks the investigation, fix design, rollout, and postmortem actions to prevent recurrence.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use hosted /v1/stream SSE endpoint with long generation (>512 tokens) and client that buffers until 'done'.
2) Introduce a TCP reset (simulated via curl --limit-rate + pkill -f client) or trigger ALB idle timeout during mid-stream,
3) Observe server-side connection close without final 'done' event, client receives truncated last chunk and attempts naive reconnect without resume token,
4) Reproduce at scale by running 200 concurrent streams and killing 10% of connections randomly to see partial_output_rate increase.
impact_summary: Affecting hosted customers only; Dedicated and Private deployments surfaced similar behaviors due to proxy/timeouts but have configuration differences. Customers experienced partial outputs that caused downstream state corruption (in-chat histories and persisted prompts), returned invalid JSON to clients, and in two cases significant user-facing failures in production flows. Business impact: multiple high-revenue customers reported degraded UX and invoked SLAs.
investigation_log: 2026-03-10: Initial triage by on-call - confirmed multiple support tickets with matching stacktraces in runtime logs (stream-connection-id present).
2026-03-11: Reproduced locally; observed race where flush-to-socket can be skipped if connection reset occurs while the final chunk is being assembled in the async buffer.

2026-03-11: Noted resume token logic stored per connection but overwritten when multiplexing internal worker tasks; when reconnects happen, resume handshake returned an older token leading to duplicate/partial replays.
2026-03-12: Identified interactions with ALB idle timeout (default 60s) and intermediate proxies in some customers' private deployments causing slightly different failure mode.
2026-03-12: Confirmed SDKs without exponential backoff or idempotency on resume cause excessive retry storms, exacerbating degraded availability during incidents.
root_cause: Two primary issues: (1) a race condition in the runtime's streaming buffer/flush path where the final token buffer could be dropped if the connection was torn down during async aggregation; (2) resume token state is not sharded correctly across worker tasks when streams are migrated, allowing the token to be stale or lost. Secondary contributor: client SDKs and some proxy defaults do not follow recommended keepalive/backoff settings, making partial failures more visible.
proposed_fixes: A) Server-side: make final token flush idempotent and durable — ensure assembled final chunks are atomically appended to persistent per-stream in-flight buffer before socket writes; on disconnect attempt graceful retransmit from buffer.

B) Server-side: partition resume-token metadata by stream UUID and pin to the originating worker; introduce a lightweight lease to prevent concurrent overwrites when a stream is migrated between workers.

C) API/SDK: add explicit resume handshake that returns last-acked token index and a small checksum; clients can request a re-stream from last-acked position. Update hosted API to support optional resume-mode header (X-Redwood-Resume: v1).
D) Operational: deploy an emergency ALB configuration change for hosted region to increase idle timeout to 180s while we roll fixes; publish temporary client guidance for keepalive and backoff.
rollback_plan: All code changes gated behind feature flag 'sse-resume-v1'. If a regression is detected in canary metrics (increase in error_rate or latency beyond threshold), flip flag off and route traffic back to prior implementation. For infra ALB timeout change, rollback by reapplying previous timeout of 60s if we observe negative side effects.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge server-side fixes behind feature flag; CI and staging verification (3/14 - 3/15).
2) Run synthetic streaming test harness with mutation (random disconnects) and validate resume_success_rate > 99% and partial_output_rate < 0.1% (3/15).
3) Canary deploy to 5% hosted traffic in us-west-2 for 24h and monitor key metrics (3/16).
4) If canary is healthy, expand to 25% then 100% over 48h with incremental SDK docs notice; keep feature flag available to roll back quickly.
5) Coordinate customer-facing patch: provide SDK release notes and Hotfix guidance to Tier 1 customers with production impact.
qa_checks: Automated unit tests for buffer flush path ensuring no-drop on close().
End-to-end SSE harness simulating client disconnects and verifying resume token correctness across worker migration scenarios.
Load test with 1000 concurrent streams and 5% induced mid-stream resets to validate stability under pressure.
Integration tests with documented proxy/ALB timeout variations to surface deployment-specific issues.
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: partial_output_rate > 0.5% for > 5m for top-10 customers -> SE on-call paging.
Dashboard: Live stream health panel with connection churn, per-worker resume token mismatches, and cumulative truncated_events counter.
mitigation_applied: Temporarily increased ALB idle timeout to 180s for hosted us-west-2 region (applied 2026-03-12).
Push to affected customers: recommended client SDK patch 1.12.4 which implements exponential backoff and resume handshake; several customers applied immediately.
Rate-limited reconnects at gateway to prevent retry storms while we investigate.
docs_and_sdk_changes: Update SDK README: recommended keepalive and backoff settings; example resume handshake flow.
Add new API header docs: X-Redwood-Resume and semantics, plus sample server responses for resume_success/failure.
Changelog entry for SDK releases: 1.12.4 and upcoming 1.13.0 with resume support.
